cards.front: What are the steps of a turn and how far ahead do you signal
cards.back: Turns start with corner searches for controls, walkers, and cars plus a signal, hold the lane nearest your direction, sight through to the farthest path point, then finish with smooth speed, a cancelled signal, and a rear check, signaling one hundred feet ahead of intersection turns and never copying a leader's blinker unless you also turn.

cards.front: From which lane edges do right and left turns start and how do multi-lane turns behave
cards.back: Right turns hug the right-most lane edge without a left swing, left turns yield to oncoming traffic from the left-most edge, and multi-lane turns pick one lane and stay married to it until done.
cards.memory_hook: Right hugs, left yields, stay married

cards.front: When is a turnabout legal and what visibility and first moves does it need
cards.back: A turnabout legally reverses direction through a street, alley, or driveway when circling the block is impractical, demanding five hundred feet of visibility each way before you signal right, stop, and check sides and rear.
cards.memory_hook: Five hundred feet, signal right, stop

cards.front: How do you back into the driveway during a turnabout
cards.back: Back to the driveway's near edge, crank fully right while creeping back, center and straighten to a stop, and on a two-lane road hug right of the center line or your own side when unmarked.

cards.front: How does a turnabout finish
cards.back: Shift to drive, check both ways, and when clear signal left into the proper lane with matching speed, mastering this move for the skills test.

cards.front: Where do right turns and left turns each launch from
cards.back: Right turns launch from the right-most lane edge, while left turns launch from the left-most edge after yielding to oncoming traffic.
cards.memory_hook: Right edge right, left edge left

cards.front: How does a driveway turnabout differ from a two-lane road turnabout
cards.back: Driveway turnabouts center the car in the drive, while two-lane turnabouts hold right of the center line or your own side.

cards.front: What do you do at every intersection and whom do you trust
cards.back: Slow at every intersection and hunt for devices, crossing traffic, walkers and cyclists, road conditions, and blind corners, trusting no one to obey or yield.

cards.front: How do you scan after stopping and what does a fresh green require
cards.back: After stopping, scan crossing traffic and bikes with a left-right-left sweep, and on a fresh green confirm a clear path plus a gap wide enough to cross, land in lane, and reach speed.

cards.front: When do you look both ways and how do you edge past blocked views
cards.back: Look both ways even when cross traffic faces red or stop signs, edge out slowly past buildings or parked rows, wait out lane-blocking views, and never nose into the next lane to peek.

cards.front: What should you never count on from other drivers
cards.back: Never count on shared space or extra room, and never trust an active turn signal, since its driver may pass you first or simply have forgotten it.

cards.front: How does traffic flow in a roundabout and who yields
cards.back: Roundabouts circle traffic counterclockwise around a raised island with entering cars yielding to circulating ones, so slow down, heed the warning sign, enter against the clock, then signal and take your exit.

cards.front: What must you do for a halted school or church bus and for how long
cards.back: Stop for any halted school or church bus loading or unloading on any roadway, since children surprise, and stay stopped until every person clears and the bus rolls.

cards.front: Which directions does the bus stop bind, what is the one exception, and what is banned
cards.back: The bus stop binds both directions on every road except opposite-side travel on a four-or-more-lane road split by an elevated barrier or unpaved median, and no vehicle may pass a bus flashing its stop arm and lights.

cards.front: What do fresh greens and facing reds each demand of you
cards.back: Fresh greens demand a patience check for crossing traffic, while reds and stops facing others still demand a both-way look.

cards.front: How broad is the bus stop rule and who alone is excused
cards.back: Bus stops bind traffic in both directions, while the lone exception frees only opposite-side drivers on a divided four-or-more-lane road.

cards.front: Where do you park safely and how does a perpendicular entry begin
cards.back: Parked cars must never menace, so use marked areas, sit far from traffic flow or tight to the curb, respect signed, painted, and colored-curb bans, and begin perpendicular entries by spotting a space, checking traffic, and signaling.

cards.front: How do you finish a perpendicular entry and exit the space
cards.back: Finish perpendicular entries by creeping centered to the space front and securing the car, and exit by backing straight until your front bumper clears the neighbor, then cranking toward the rear's path before driving off smooth and straight.
cards.memory_hook: Center in, back till bumper clears

cards.front: How does a parallel entry begin and how far do you reverse
cards.back: Parallel entries start with space, traffic, and signal, then reverse while gazing rearward with quick wheel work until your front bumper lines with the lead car's rear bumper.

cards.front: How do you settle into a parallel slot and leave the car legally
cards.back: Center into the slot, stop short of the rear bumper, drive-adjust, immobilize with brake and park or reverse gear, slip out curbside, and obey the law: engine off, key out, doors locked.

cards.front: How do you exit a parallel space
cards.back: Parallel exits brake and back toward the rear car, then check, signal, and drive forward into the lane once the door post clears the lead car's rear bumper, re-reversing short of clearance, a maneuver to master for skills day.

cards.front: How do you park on a hill and secure the car
cards.back: Aim hill-parked wheels to catch the curb if you roll, or off the road where curbless, then kill the engine, pocket the key, and lock up even for short stops.
cards.memory_hook: Wheels to curb, key out, lock

cards.front: Who may use handicapped bays and where do applicants get decals
cards.back: Handicapped bays serve only permitted vehicles carrying a disabled person, with violators fined and applicants directed to the County Clerk for decals or plates.

cards.front: How do the perpendicular exit cue and the parallel entry cue differ
cards.back: Perpendicular exits back straight until the front bumper clears, while parallel entries reverse until the front bumper aligns.

cards.front: What do hill parking and every stop each require
cards.back: Hill parking aims wheels at the curb or off the road, while every stop ends with engine off, key out, and doors locked.

cards.front: What are the lane roles on multi-lane and two-lane roads and what left-lane habit is illegal
cards.back: Three-or-more lanes give middles to through traffic, the left to passers and left-turners, and the right to slower, entering, and right-turning drivers, while two-lane roads flow smoothest right with the left saved for passing, and camping the left lane of a limited-access highway breaks the law.
cards.memory_hook: Middle through, left pass, right slow

cards.front: Which lane do you turn into, what if you miss a turn, and what once committed
cards.back: Turn into your nearest lane, with multi-lane lefts starting nearest center and rights nearest curb before any later change, loop around when you miss a turn, and follow through once committed in an intersection since last-second swerves collide.

cards.front: How does a lane change begin
cards.back: Lane changes open with mirrors and an over-the-shoulder blind-spot check toward your move.

cards.front: How do you complete a lane change
cards.back: Complete the change by spotting a gap, signaling, glancing again, and steering in at matched speed.

cards.front: How do you join a freeway and who has the right of way
cards.back: Join freeways via the acceleration lane at traffic speed through a chosen gap with a cancelled signal, yielding to traffic already there.

cards.front: How do you plan and execute a freeway exit
cards.back: Plan exits early by sliding to the exit lane, holding highway speed, then signaling into the deceleration lane and slowing to its posted limit.
cards.memory_hook: Exit lane early, slow in deceleration

cards.front: How do multi-lane roles differ from the two-lane rule
cards.back: Three-or-more lanes split through, pass, and slow roles, while two-lane roads keep the left purely for passing.

cards.front: What do you do about a missed turn versus a committed turn
cards.back: Missed turns loop around at the next intersection, while committed turns follow through without last-second swerves.

cards.front: How do freeway entries and exits differ in speed handling
cards.back: Highway entries speed up in the acceleration lane and yield to existing flow, while exits hold speed and then slow in the deceleration lane.
cards.memory_hook: Entry speeds up, exit slows after

cards.front: On which side do you pass, when may you pass right, and when may you leave the roadway
cards.back: Pass on the left as a rule with the left-most lane reserved for it, pass right only when truly safe since right-side cars hide and surprise, and never leave the roadway unless the passed car fully stops and the move stays safe.
cards.memory_hook: Pass left, right rarely, stay on

cards.front: What do solid and broken lines permit and when must a pass be finished
cards.back: A solid line on your side of a broken line bans passing while a solid yellow left of a broken yellow permits it with no oncoming traffic and sign approval, and Kentucky law demands the pass finish before any no-passing zone and before closing within two hundred feet of oncoming cars.

cards.front: What is the passing sequence and when do you return
cards.back: Pass briskly yet safely with oncoming, mirror, and shoulder checks plus a signal, glide over at adjusted speed, hold out until the passed car's full front fills your rearview, signal back, and merge smooth.

cards.front: Where should you never start a pass
cards.back: Weigh space at hills, curves, intersections, and obstacles, treat every blind hill or curve as hiding oncoming traffic and never start there, and shun passing near crossroads, crowds, shops, schools, parks, and crossings where blocked views and side entries ambush.

cards.front: When do you pull out to pass, when do you return, and how much room do bikes get
cards.back: Pull out only with room to return, declining multi-car gambles and borrowed space, and return once the passed car shows in your outside mirror; give same-direction bikes and scooters a full left-lane shift when lanes allow or three feet of left-side room on single lanes, cross the center even past no-passing paint when the left runs clear, and stay cautious when three feet will not fit.
cards.memory_hook: Room to return, three feet bikes

cards.front: What do you do when another driver overtakes you
cards.back: When overtaken, hold your lane, and Kentucky law orders you to yield right to the passer while all road users cooperate for clearance.

cards.front: Which line bans your pass and which permits it
cards.back: A solid line on your side bans the pass, while a solid yellow left of the broken yellow permits it.
cards.memory_hook: Solid your side bans, broken permits

cards.front: How does returning from a car pass differ from passing a bike
cards.back: Car passes return once the passed car fills the outside mirror, while bike passes keep three feet of left-side room throughout.
cards.memory_hook: Mirror cue cars, three feet bikes

recap_hooks.text: Signal early, right hugs, left yields, turnabout needs sight
Slow and scan, trust no one, yield in roundabouts, stop for buses
Park safe, bumpers guide, hill wheels curb, lock up
Lanes have roles, nearest lane, shoulder check, accelerate to merge
Pass left, read lines, mirror cue, three feet for bikes
